title: Challenge — FX Rates, Parity & the Yen Carry
description: Harder follow-up to the FX fundamentals: interest-rate parity, forward pricing, rollover, drawdown math, and yen intervention. Verify any live figures before trading.

questions.prompt: Covered interest rate parity says the FX forward rate is pinned by:

options: The interest-rate differential between the two currencies

questions.explanation: CIP: the forward is the spot adjusted by the two currencies' interest-rate differential; otherwise riskless arbitrage exists.

questions.prompt: Under interest-rate parity, a currency whose interest rate is HIGHER than the other typically trades at a forward:
questions.explanation: The higher-yielding currency trades at a forward discount, offsetting the rate advantage so covered arbitrage nets to zero.

questions.prompt: Holding a long USD/JPY position overnight while USD rates exceed JPY rates usually produces:

options: A margin call regardless of price

questions.explanation: You are long the higher-yield currency (USD) vs the lower-yield (JPY), so the rollover/swap accrues in your favor — the carry.

questions.prompt: Uncovered interest rate parity is strongly supported by short-run empirical data.
questions.explanation: The 'forward premium puzzle': high-rate currencies have historically tended to appreciate short-run, contradicting UIP — the basis of carry profits.

questions.prompt: A position that has lost 50% of its value must subsequently gain how much to break even?
questions.explanation: From 100 to 50 is -50%; 50 back to 100 is +100%. Drawdowns are asymmetric, which is why capital preservation dominates.

questions.prompt: Which Japanese government body directs yen FX intervention (executed operationally by the BOJ)?
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Finance decides on intervention; the Bank of Japan executes it as the MOF's agent.

questions.prompt: All else equal, a trader's risk of ruin rises most sharply when they:

options: Lower leverage and risk a small fixed fraction per trade
Increase position size relative to account equity
Use a fixed stop-loss on every trade

questions.explanation: Risk of ruin grows with per-trade risk fraction (position size / equity); oversizing dominates even a positive-edge strategy.

questions.prompt: Explain the mechanics of a yen carry-trade unwind: what triggers it, and how interest-rate expectations and the JPY exchange rate interact to amplify losses.

payload.rubric: Describes funding in cheap JPY into higher-yield assets; trigger = JPY appreciation or rate-gap narrowing / risk-off; feedback loop of forced deleveraging buying back JPY, accelerating the move.
